headline: The yellow bomb makes you earn the kill
lede: Missile Battle's smart bomb now reads the sky: a short-fused blast converging on it provokes a committed sideways jink, once per bomb. The first interceptor is a feint that learns where it runs; the next round is aimed at the escape. Fully deterministic — same sky, same jink, every replay.

notes.text: Main went red on the nightly (worktreepurgecheck's sandbox merge died on the runner's missing git identity, stderr hidden). Two lanes filed the fix simultaneously; the shipped one pinned GIT_* identity in the fixture and made failures print git's actual reason. Repro was exact: the hostile-config run mirrored CI's tally line for line.

The jink rule lives entirely in the sim (CFG.dodge + dodgeOn mutant switch) — the autopilot planner needed zero changes: it re-aims from live state, so the escape costs exactly one extra round per smart bomb and the slack rule still wins all three waves at 9 per battery.

missilecheck grew a JINK section: no-jink on a quiet sky, no-jink at far-aimed missiles, escape direction away from the detonation point, survival outside the blast reach, spent-budget follow-up kill, 5/5 smart bombs join the real fight — plus three named mutants that all die by name.

Never-dry pick after audit exclusions: Britannia's top score was adjudicated stage-2-only by the live audit, BoulderDash and Sonar gaps were owned by fresh QA passes — the honest weakest unowned gap on the shelf became this dodge.
